# Pull GBIF / iDigBio occurrence data

To get started, we're going to be pulling code from the [Soltis lab
ENM Botany 2025 workshop](https://soltislab.github.io/BotanyENMWorkshops/Botany2025/Botany2025.html). 

## package management

### download packages

```{r eval = FALSE}
library(devtools)
list_of_packages <- c(
  # Core ENM tools
  "terra", "dismo", "ENMeval", "ENMTools", "biomod2",
  # Spatial / Mapping
  "sf", "rnaturalearth", "ggspatial", "leaflet",
  "fields", "rangeBuilder",
  # Visualization
  "ggplot2", "viridis", "gridExtra",
  # Data manipulation
  "dplyr", "tidyr", "stringr", "gtools",
  # Phylogenetics
  "ape", "phytools",
  # Biodiversity data
  "ridigbio", "gatoRs",
  # Other utilities
  "multcompView", "usdm", "predicts", "rJava"
)

new.packages <- list_of_packages[!(list_of_packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]

if (length(new.packages)) {
  cat("\nInstalling missing CRAN packages:\n")
  print(new.packages)
  install.packages(new.packages)
} else {
  cat("\nAll required CRAN packages already installed.\n")
}

## ---- Load All CRAN Packages ----

# Try loading all required CRAN packages.
loaded <- sapply(list_of_packages, require, character.only = TRUE)

if (any(!loaded)) {
  cat("\nWARNING: These CRAN packages failed to load:\n")
  print(list_of_packages[!loaded])
} else {
  cat("\nAll CRAN packages loaded successfully.\n")
}

github_repos <- c(
  "vqv/ggbiplot"
)

for (repo in github_repos) {
  pkg <- tail(strsplit(repo, "/")[[1]], 1)
  if (!pkg %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"]) {
    cat(paste("\nInstalling GitHub package:", repo, "\n"))
    devtools::install_github(repo, upgrade = "never")
  } else {
    cat(paste("\nGitHub package already installed:", pkg, "\n"))
  }
}

# Try loading GitHub packages.
github_packages <- c("ggbiplot")
github_loaded <- sapply(github_packages, require, character.only = TRUE)

if (any(!github_loaded)) {
  cat("\nWARNING: These GitHub packages failed to load:\n")
  print(github_packages[!github_loaded])
} else {
  cat("\nAll GitHub packages loaded successfully.\n")
}
```

no failed taxa, no no-data taxa. cool!

## pull species-level occurrences for infraspecific taxa

For all taxa sampled at the infraspecific level, pull occurrences once at the species level using `species_synonymdict` (built in `clean_taxonomy.qmd`). Unlike pooling the synonym lists of the subspecies we sampled, this includes the species name itself, the accepted infraspecific taxa we *didn't* sample, and the synonyms of the species as a whole. Filicaulis is intentionally excluded (subspp. kept separate).

```{julia}
#| eval: false
# filicaulis subspp. are kept separate
species_taxa = filter(sp_name -> !occursin("filicaulis", sp_name), sort(collect(keys(species_synonymdict))))
species_pulled = pull_occurrences(species_synonymdict, raw_dir; taxa=species_taxa)
```

## grab non research grade Cocucci/Sersic iNat obs.

the python for this lives in `scripts/pull_nonresearch_inat.py` and is run as a script: running it line by line in the
interactive python console splits the loops at their blank lines, which silently keeps only the last observation.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
run(`python3 scripts/pull_nonresearch_inat.py`)
```

## clean occurrence data

batch cleaning for all species:
```{julia}
# Load homonyms file: names that are used for more than one taxon, under different authorities
homonyms = DataFrame(CSV.File("data/taxonomy_trait_data/homonyms.csv"))

# clean both the taxa as sampled & the species-level pulls for taxa sampled at the infraspecific level
all_synonymdict = merge(synonymdict, species_synonymdict)

# For each taxon, collect the homonyms ("name authority") that belong to a *different* taxon,
# so we can filter them out of that taxon's occurrences.
# Example: "Calceolaria nitida" has the synonym "Calceolaria glandulosa Benth.",
#          so when processing "Calceolaria nitida", filter OUT "Calceolaria glandulosa Poepp. ex Benth." (a valid name!)
# Example: "Calceolaria meyeniana" has the synonym "Calceolaria cheiranthoides Reiche ex Witasek",
#          so filter OUT "Calceolaria cheiranthoides Phil. ex Reiche" (a synonym of dentata subsp. dentata)
homonyms_to_exclude = find_homonyms_to_exclude(all_synonymdict, homonyms)

println("Taxa with homonyms to filter: $(length(homonyms_to_exclude))")
for taxa in sort(collect(keys(homonyms_to_exclude)))
    println("  $taxa will EXCLUDE: $(join(homonyms_to_exclude[taxa], "; "))")
end
```

```{julia}
filtering_stats = clean_occurrences(
    all_synonymdict,
    raw_dir,
    "data/occurrence_data/pt_occs_clean",
    "data/occurrence_data/pt_occs_to_georeference";
    homonyms_to_exclude=homonyms_to_exclude,
    # remove points above or below lat/long bounding box
    lat_min=-56, lat_max=31.5,
    lon_min=-117, lon_max=-33,
    # some parts of texas fall into this range above so let's manually remove USA pts
    countries_to_remove=["United States of America"],
    drop_missing_country=true
)
#fixit: incorporate native range polygons?
```

### check minimum number of occurrences
```{julia}
# add calculated columns for seeing filtering before and after nrow
filtering_stats.taxa_clean_removed = filtering_stats.raw .- filtering_stats.after_taxa_clean
filtering_stats.duplicates_removed = filtering_stats.after_taxa_clean .- filtering_stats.after_remove_duplicates
filtering_stats.total_removed = filtering_stats.raw .- filtering_stats.after_remove_duplicates
filtering_stats.percent_retained = round.((filtering_stats.after_remove_duplicates ./ filtering_stats.raw) .* 100, digits=1)

# show taxa with filtering
filtered_taxa = filtering_stats[filtering_stats.total_removed .> 0, :]
println("Taxa with records removed ($(nrow(filtered_taxa)) taxa):")
println(filtered_taxa)

# save the stats
#CSV.write("data/filtering_stats_2026_02_18.csv", filtering_stats)
#println("\nFiltering statistics saved to data/filtering_stats_2026_02_18.csv")
```

create priority list for georeferencing:
```{julia}
# sort descending on rows missing coords (prioritizing rows w/ many we can georeference)
sort!(filtering_stats, :rows_missing_coords, rev=true)
# sort ascending on rows with very few coords as is (w/ lat/longs)
sort!(filtering_stats, :after_locality_filt, rev=false)
# separate out those where the sum of :rows_missing_coords + :after_locality_filt < 15 (not as much of a priority)
toofewobs = filter(row -> row.rows_missing_coords + row.after_locality_filt < 15, filtering_stats)
enoughobs = filter(row -> row.rows_missing_coords + row.after_locality_filt >= 15, filtering_stats)
CSV.write("data/occurrence_data/summarytables_plots/ranked_togeoref.csv", enoughobs)
```

## oct 2026- merge already geolocated lines into the species-level geolocate files

the species-level pulls include records that were already georeferenced (or looked at & marked `VIABLE` = FALSE) for
their infraspecific taxa. this copies those rows' coordinates, notes & `VIABLE` into the species-level geolocate files
(matching on `ID`), so only the rows with an empty `VIABLE` still need to be looked at.

```{julia}
geolocate_dir = "data/occurrence_data/pt_occs_to_georeference_geolocate_format"
georef_dir = "data/occurrence_data/pt_occs_georeferenced"

for species in sort(collect(keys(species_synonymdict)))
    stem = replace(species, " " => "_")
    geolocate_path = latest_no_coords_file(stem, geolocate_dir)
    isempty(geolocate_path) && continue

    # georeferenced files of this species' infraspecific taxa
    infra_files = filter(f -> startswith(taxon_stem(f), stem * "_"), readdir(georef_dir))
    isempty(infra_files) && continue
    georef_df = vcat([read_georef_file(joinpath(georef_dir, f)) for f in infra_files]...; cols=:union)

    filled, n_filled = carry_over_georef(read_occs(geolocate_path), georef_df)
    CSV.write(geolocate_path, filled)
    println("$species: $n_filled of $(nrow(filled)) rows already looked at ($(count(isequal("TRUE"), filled.VIABLE)) viable), from $(length(infra_files)) file(s)")
end
```
